headlines.title: Anthropic's S-1 is out. Is it actually making money?
headlines.summary: Anthropic just filed its S-1 ahead of what could be the biggest IPO in history, and the headline number is an $80.7 billion loss. Host Ejaaz Ahamadeen goes through the filing, from revenue that hit $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 to $132 billion in cash, and why most of that loss isn't cash out the door.

headlines.title: Qualcomm Just Dropped 13% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell, or Load Up?
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysQualcomm (QCOM:NASDAQ) stock dropped 13% in the month through October 22, with a September 28 semiconductor selloff accounting for more than half the decline. Arm Holdings (ARM:NASDAQ) fell 37% over the same period, compared with the Nasdaq 100’s 6% decline, highlighting broader semiconductor weakness.

headlines.title: Arm Holdings (ARM) Faces Jury Breach Ruling As It Unveils Server Security Tie Up
headlines.summary: Arm Holdings (NasdaqGS:ARM) was found by a jury to have breached its longstanding Architectural License Agreement with Qualcomm. The jury also concluded that Arm intentionally acted to disrupt Qualcomm's business in connection with the disputed licensing arrangements. Separately, Arm announced a collaboration with Axiado to integrate secure control modules into its AGI CPU server platform for data centers.

headlines.title: Is QUALCOMM (QCOM) Undervalued After Reaffirming Its Dividend?
headlines.summary: QUALCOMM (QCOM) reaffirmed its quarterly cash dividend, maintaining the payout at US$0.92 per share for stockholders of record on December 3, with payment scheduled for December 17, 2026. QUALCOMM shares trade at US$175.91, with a 1-day share price return of 1.78% and a 7-day gain of 1.37%. The 30-day share price return is down 12.9%, suggesting near term momentum has cooled. However, the 3-year total shareholder return of 73.83% and 5-year total shareholder return of 45.

description: QUALCOMM Incorporated engages in the development and commercialization of foundational technologies for the wireless industry worldwide. It operates through three segments: Qualcomm CDMA Technologies (QCT); Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL); and Qualcomm Strategic Initiatives (QSI). The QCT segment develops and supplies integrated circuits and system software with connectivity and computing technologies for use in mobile devices; automotive systems for connectivity, digital cockpit, and ADAS/AD; and IoT, including consumer electronic devices, industrial devices, and edge networking products. The QTL segment grants licenses or provides rights to use portions of its intellectual property portfolio, which include various patent rights useful in the manufacture and sale of wireless products comprising products implementing LTE, and/or OFDMA-based 5G products and derivatives; to use cellular standard-essential patents, including 3G, 4G and 5G for cellular devices. The QSI segment invests in early-stage companies in various industries, including 5G, artificial intelligence, automotive, consumer, enterprise, cloud, IoT, and extended reality, and investments, including non-marketable equity securities and, to a lesser extent, marketable equity securities, and convertible debt instruments. It also provides development, and other services and sells related products to the United States government agencies and their contractors. In addition, the company is also involved in Qualcomm government technologies and data center businesses. Further, it provides security and intelligence services for unmanaged networks through software-based network security solutions. The company is in collaboration with Amazon to enable customized silicon at scale for large-scale AI data centers. QUALCOMM Incorporated was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in San Diego, California.
